subject: BrightLane: pricing worksheet & commitment options
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@brightlane.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLane: pricing worksheet & commitment options

Hi Alyssa — great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum:  

- Recap: BrightLane is evaluating an LLM-powered triage assistant for clinical intake. Primary constraints are predictable unit cost, SOC2 evidence, and a pilot budget window for Q3.
- What we asked you on the call: expected token profile (avg tokens per request), peak vs baseline traffic, and budget range for a sustained pilot. You mentioned 20–30k requests/day, ~1.2k average tokens per request (range 400–2,800).
- Immediate next steps (for this week): 1) I’ll share a pricing workbook with committed-use tiers + starter credits, 2) you confirm an internal budget range and whether procurement will require a PO or signed MSA, 3) we schedule an optional exec/technical sync with your CTO if the numbers look good.

Attached: BrightLane_pricing_workbook_2026-07-15.xlsx (pricing scenarios + unit economics calculator). Also attaching our SOC2 summary for procurement.

A couple of initial scenarios I populated in the workbook (see tab "quick view") — feel free to overwrite with your real monthly volume: 
- Low pilot: 10M tokens / month -> list price estimate ~ $1,200 per 1M tokens (no commit) -> ~ $12k/mo
- Pilot w/ 12mo commit (20M/mo): target net $/1M tokens in workbook shows $780 with a 12-mo commit + startup credit offer.
- 24mo / multi-year: deeper discounts available (we model up to 30% off list with multi-year & minimums).

Ask from you: the single number that matters to procurement is a target $/1M tokens that keeps you inside your budget ceiling. If you can share your target (range is fine), I’ll highlight the specific line in the workbook and propose a formal committed-use proposal.

If easier, propose two outcomes: (A) light pilot (no commit) to validate model quality, or (B) pilot with a modest commit to secure unit economics and a startup discount. We can map both to the workbook.

Availability to follow up: Thurs 10–11am PT or Fri 9–12pm PT.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightLane_pricing_workbook_2026-07-15.xlsx (XLSX), SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf (PDF)

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@brightlane.health>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.health
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane: pricing worksheet & commitment options

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the recap and the workbook. Quick answers from our side:  

- Volume: based on the initial product scope, we’re estimating 15–25M tokens/month for the pilot (roughly 15–20k requests/day at the token counts we discussed). Peak could spike to ~40M in month 3 if adoption is strong.
- Budget: our finance sponsor gave a hard pilot ceiling of $9k–$11k/month (we know this is tight). That’s why we’re prioritizing net $/1M tokens to see if a committed tier could get us in range.
- Procurement asks: SOC2 evidence and a short MSA or SOW; PO is possible but procurement prefers having an MSA in place first. Procurement copied here (procurement@brightlane.health).

On discounts: we’re a seed-stage startup (Series A in 2025) and would like to request any startup program credits + a committed-use discount. Ideally we’re targeting <= $700 per 1M tokens net to hit the budget at expected volumes, or a combination of credits + commit that gets us into that band.

Happy to review the workbook — can you surface a couple commitment scenarios that hit ~$700/1M (or the closest option) and the minimum term + spend required? If a 12-month is needed to reach that price we’d need to confirm internally but are open to discussion.

I can meet Fri 11am PT to go through specifics and procurement questions.

Best,
Alyssa Turner
Head of Product
BrightLane Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@brightlane.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@brightlane.health
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane: pricing worksheet & commitment options

Alyssa — thanks for the clarity; that helps a lot. I updated the workbook and added two highlighted commitment scenarios (see attached). TL;DR options that come close to your target: 

Scenario A — 12 month commit (20M tokens/mo average)
- Gross unit list: $1,050 / 1M tokens
- Redwood 12-mo committed discount: 25% -> $787 / 1M
- Startup program credit (one-time applied over first 3 months): equivalent to additional ~10% reduction across Q1 -> effective averaged net ~ $710 / 1M in year 1
- Minimum committed spend: $150k over 12 months (we model 20M/mo for 12 months)

Scenario B — 24 month commit (min 15M tokens/mo)
- Gross unit list: $1,050 / 1M
- Redwood multi-year incentive: 32% -> $714 / 1M
- Startup program credit (applied): additional $40k credit front-loaded -> effective net ~ $645 / 1M year 1
- Minimum committed spend: $350k over 24 months

Notes: the workbook has a sensitivity tab where you can plug in exact monthly ramps (month-by-month). I purposely left the workbook conservative on token compression and cache benefits; if your real workload benefits from more prefix reuse we can improve unit economics.

Next steps I propose: 1) you confirm which scenario (A or B) is directionally preferred, 2) I’ll prepare a redlined MSA + commercial sheet for procurement showing the exact credit amortization and payment terms, 3) technical validation: optional 30-min call between your CTO and our Solutions Architect (Monica) to validate inference latency & kv cache assumptions.

I’m attaching the updated workbook and SOC2 summary again for procurement.

Availability: Fri 11am PT works for me to walk the workbook.

—Marcus

Attachments: BrightLane_pricing_workbook_2026-07-16.xlsx (XLSX), SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf (PDF)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightLane commercial options (internal)

Forwarding for internal ops notes — quick checklist for Marcus: 

- Validate minimums in the workbook before sending to procurement — confirm 20M/mo average is defensible (Alyssa said 15–25M). If they choose scenario A we should propose a quarterly true-up clause to accommodate ramp.
- Confirm startup program approval route: I’ll engage Growth to sign off on the startup credit amount (we typically offer 40–60k in credits for Series A with pilot commitments).
- Payment terms + PO: procurement asked about PO vs signed MSA. Recommend we offer a 30-day invoice for first 3 months, then net-30 for remainder (or annual prepay discount option).
- Legal: I’ll attach MA_template_redlined.pdf to the hubspot deal and request our legal ops to pre-populate the signature block for quick turnaround.

I’ll loop in Growth and Legal if Marcus gives the go-ahead to present scenario A/B to the customer tomorrow.

—Ben

Attachments: MA_template_redlined.pdf

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@brightlane.health>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.health, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2026 09:21:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane: pricing worksheet & commitment options

Thanks Marcus & team — appreciate the fast turnaround and transparent scenarios. We reviewed internally and procurement is comfortable pursuing Scenario A (12-mo commit) conditional on: 

1) startup credit of $50k applied up front to the first 3 invoices;
2) a quarterly true-up mechanism for usage variance;
3) SOC2 evidence and MSA with standard data protection addendum.

Procurement will prepare a PO once the MSA is in good order; I’ll confirm internal sponsor sign-off next week. Let’s use Fri 11am PT to do a final numbers walk — I’ll invite our finance sponsor and CTO.

Looking forward — Alyssa
